learnings.question: What personal business lesson holds that wealth should come as a natural byproduct of doing right by people, rather than being the main goal itself?
options: Aggressively maximizing profit margins above all else
Acting with honesty in trade and doing right by people, without chasing wealth as the primary goal
Finding every legal loophole available to get richer faster
Focusing solely on investor returns before anything else
learnings.learning: Going into business to do what's right by people, with honesty in trade, lets wealth come naturally as a byproduct, rather than treating wealth itself as the goal.

learnings.question: Which idea holds that hard work does not directly cause success, but instead widens a person's 'surface area' for opportunity to find them?
options: Hard work correlates with success rather than causing it
Hard work guarantees financial success eventually
Talent matters more than effort in determining outcomes
Success is entirely random and unrelated to effort
learnings.learning: Hard work doesn't cause success outright; it correlates with it by widening the surface area for opportunity to meet you, so it shouldn't be called the sole cause of success or failure.

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, what term refers to humanity's role as steward or caretaker of the Earth?
learnings.learning: Muslims are described as khalifah (caretakers) of the Earth, a role that carries responsibility beyond personal actions toward preserving faith and fostering unity.

learnings.question: Which set of three roles is described as life's primary purposes in a framework drawn from the Quran and Hadith?
options: Worship, stewardship (khalifah) of the Earth, and living life as a test of faith and conduct
learnings.learning: Life's purpose is framed around three roles: worshiping Allah, serving as khalifah (caretaker) of the Earth, and living as a test of faith and conduct that shapes one's eternal outcome.

learnings.question: In a word-frequency analysis of the Quran's full Arabic text, what share of the Quran's total word count did the 20 most frequent words account for?
learnings.learning: A word-frequency analysis of the Quran found that the top 20 most frequent words accumulate to only about 20.83% of the text, so the 80/20 Pareto principle doesn't hold here.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: What term describes the small diacritical markings placed above or below Arabic letters to indicate vowel sounds?
learnings.learning: Tashkeel are the small markings added above or below Arabic letters to show which vowel sound to use; without them, reading Arabic becomes trickier since the bare letters don't indicate pronunciation.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, which term refers to the actual unfolding of events in a person's life, as shaped by their actions and decisions?
learnings.learning: Qada' refers to the actual occurrence of events in a person's life, shaped by their actions and decisions, while Qadr is Allah's complete, eternal plan encompassing all events.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: What's a common misconception about how supplication (dua) changes a person's circumstances?
options: That dua has no real effect on daily circumstances
That dua can only affect the Hereafter, never this life
That dua only counts if recited after a prescribed prayer
That the change happens outside of, or unknown to, Allah's prior knowledge
learnings.learning: Even though sincere dua can change one's Qada' (circumstances), that change was always already known to Allah and encompassed within His Qadr, since He is All-Knowing.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: Which thinker is credited with the 1971 observation that an information-rich world creates 'a scarcity of attention'?
learnings.learning: Herbert Simon observed in 1971 that in an information-rich world, the wealth of information creates a scarcity of attention, since information consumes the attention of whoever receives it.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: What single screening question was used to automatically filter a personal YouTube content feed down to only worthwhile videos?
options: Would a Muslim, Malaysian software engineer early in his career actually benefit from watching this?
Was this video uploaded in the last 24 hours?
Does this channel have over 100,000 subscribers?
Is this video under 10 minutes long?
learnings.learning: A daily script pulls videos from hand-picked YouTube channels and uses AI to filter them with one question: would a Muslim, Malaysian software engineer early in his career actually benefit from watching this?
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: In the Scrum framework, which artifact visualizes a sprint's progress and shows how much work remains?
learnings.learning: The Burndown Chart is a Scrum artifact that visualizes the progress of the sprint, showing remaining work and helping the team track whether they're on schedule.

learnings.question: In Scrum, what is the primary focus of the Sprint Review ceremony?
options: Assigning daily tasks to individual developers
Demonstrating completed work to the Product Owner and reflecting on improvements for future sprints
Planning the entire project timeline up front
Writing the initial product backlog from scratch
learnings.learning: The Sprint Review is the ceremony where the team demonstrates completed work to the Product Owner and reflects on the sprint to discuss improvements for future sprints.

learnings.question: Which 19th-century researcher showed that people forget roughly 80% of what they learn within 24 hours unless they actively recall it?
learnings.learning: Back in the 1880s, Hermann Ebbinghaus proved that we forget about 80% of what we learn within 24 hours unless we actively force ourselves to recall it, which is why re-reading notes doesn't work as well as being quizzed.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: What personal problem motivated building an automated daily trivia quiz out of one's own old blog posts?
options: Testing out a new AI model's capabilities
Needing content ideas for new blog posts
Wanting more pageviews on old articles
Forgetting the lessons from articles shortly after writing them
learnings.learning: The habit of writing something down, feeling enlightened, and then completely forgetting it by the next day led to building a script that quizzes on old articles every morning using spaced repetition.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: In PCIe power management, which state represents the device being almost completely powered down, used for the longest periods of inactivity with the highest power savings?
learnings.learning: L2 is the deepest PCIe power management state, where the device is almost completely powered down, giving the highest power savings but also the longest wake-up time.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe
